title: What If You Grew One Metre Every Day?
description:
What if you grew one metre taller every single day, and never stopped? Day by day, from your own street to the summit of Mount Everest: what your bones, your heart, your nerves and the air around your head would go through.

The premise is impossible. The heights, weights and physics are real. 3D city scenes made in Blender with CC0 assets by Quaternius and Kenney.
core_message: Growing a metre a day, you'd outgrow your own skeleton within days and reach Everest's height in 24 years.
comment_question: Which day would you have wanted it to stop?

scenes.narration: Day eight thousand, eight hundred and forty seven. Your head is level with the top of Mount Everest.
What if you grew one metre taller, every single day, and never stopped?
Day zero. One point seven metres. An ordinary morning, on an ordinary street.
Day one. You wake up two point seven metres tall. Your bed, your clothes and your door no longer fit.
That's the height of Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever recorded. He needed leg braces to walk.
Here's why. Grow twice as tall and you weigh eight times as much. Your bones are only four times as thick.
It's called the square-cube law. Every day, each bone carries more weight than the day before.
Day four. Five point seven metres. You're looking a giraffe in the eye.
A giraffe needs about twice your blood pressure to get blood up to its brain. Your heart has to keep up.
Day nine. Ten metres. Taller than a two-storey house, and people stop in the street to stare.
Day sixteen. You weigh around eighty tonnes. As much as a dozen elephants.
Day twenty three. You're taller than every house on the street. People run when you turn around.
Day forty. You weigh about a thousand tonnes. As much as seven hundred cars.
Day ninety one. Ninety three metres. As tall as the Statue of Liberty, pedestal and torch included.
One step now crosses a whole city block. Traffic stops wherever you stand.
Day two hundred. Every tower in the old town is below your chin.
Day three hundred and sixty five. One year in, and you're three hundred and sixty seven metres tall.
Taller than the Empire State Building, antenna and all.
Day eight hundred and twenty six. You look the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa, in the eye.
Your nerves carry signals at about a hundred metres a second. A message from your toes now takes ten seconds.
Stub your toe, and you'll feel it fifteen seconds later.
Day two thousand five hundred. Almost seven years. Low clouds start drifting around your knees.
Day three thousand, seven hundred and seventy four. You're as tall as Mount Fuji.
The air around your head gets colder as you rise. About six and a half degrees for every kilometre.
Your face is now in air almost forty degrees colder than the street under your feet.
And thinner. Up here, every breath holds less than half the air it did on the street.
Below you, the city you grew up in would fit in the palm of your hand.
Day eight thousand, eight hundred and forty seven. Twenty four years. You're as tall as Mount Everest.
At the summit, the air is a third as thick as on your street, and nearly sixty degrees colder.
A message from your toes takes a minute and a half to arrive.
And tomorrow, you'll be one metre taller still.
Somewhere far below, the street where it started is still there. You just can't see it any more.
